dataset_name: GBD 2019 relative risks for high systolic blood pressure

description_and_role: Age-specific relative risk per 10 mmHg higher SBP by cause. Used to distribute each country-age-sex-cause baseline incidence rate across the 8 SBP categories (the alpha normalisation in calculate_baseline_incidence_gbd), i.e. it sets the BP-bin-specific incidence structure on which the sodium effect operates.
variables_used: Risk-Outcome; age-group RR columns 20-24 years through 95+ years (reshaped to rr_per_10mmhg). Dropped on read: Category / Units; Morbidity / Mortality; Sex; All-age; all age columns below 20-24.
geographic_coverage: Global (no country dimension; the same RR schedule is applied to every modelled country)
age_coverage: 20-95; GBD 5-year groups expanded to single-year ages (20-24 set equal to 25-29)
sex_coverage: Both sexes combined (Sex column dropped; single RR schedule used for male and female)
time_coverage: GBD 2019 estimation round; time-invariant in the model
unit_of_observation: risk-outcome (cause) x age group
source_institution: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME)
original_source_publication: GBD 2019 relative risks release (file stamp Y2020M10D15), high-SBP risk-outcome pairs
update_frequency_or_reference_version: GBD relative-risk release (GBD 2019 used here; IHME re-releases per GBD round)
processing_notes_assumptions_limitations: Cell range A3:AB20 is hard-coded, so any change in workbook layout silently mis-parses. RR strings are parsed with a regex that keeps the point estimate and discards the uncertainty interval, so no RR uncertainty enters the model. Only ihd, istroke, hstroke and hhd are retained. RRs are treated as log-linear per 10 mmHg when scaled by 0.1 x sbp_reduction. Note the baseline rates are GBD 2023-derived while these RRs are GBD 2019.
manual_confirmation_needed: GHDX record / citation URL for the exact release; whether GBD 2019 RRs should be updated to match the GBD 2023 baseline
